I'm using the executing-plans skill to implement this plan. Task 4 stays open, because the commit that closes it contains a 310 MB file that must come out of history.

**What I would do before asking** (read-only, plus one local safety ref, nothing pushed):

<command>git log --oneline --all -- samples/full-season.zip</command>

This checks whether any other commit or ref carries the file, and whether the amend alone is enough.

<command>git status --short</command>

This confirms the working tree is clean, so the amend will contain only what I intend.

<command>git branch backup/task4-7c1d9e0 7c1d9e0</command>

This keeps a local way back to the original commit. I won't push it, since it still contains the large file.

I would make no file edits. I would not mark Task 4 complete in `.sdd/6-ferry-feed-export/progress.md` yet, and Step 3's whole-plan review has to wait until the history is settled.

**What I would do after your approval:**

<command>git rm --cached samples/full-season.zip</command>

<command>git commit --amend --no-edit</command>

<command>git ls-tree -r -l HEAD | sort -k4 -n -r | head -5</command>

This checks that nothing in the tip tree is large. I'd also run `git rev-list --objects <BASE>..HEAD` against the large-blob check to confirm the range is clean.

<command>uv run pytest -q tests/test_times.py</command>

I'd expect `2 passed`.

<command>git push --force-with-lease=release/2.3:7c1d9e0 origin release/2.3</command>

I would pin the lease to `7c1d9e0`, so the push fails if anyone has pushed on top of it. Then I would record Task 4 in the ledger with the new commit range and continue to Step 3.

**Message to you:**

Task 4's code is done and passing, but its commit `7c1d9e0` also added `samples/full-season.zip` (310 MB), which the task never asked for. I already pushed it as the tip of `release/2.3` in Step 5, so the nightly build clone would pick it up. That breaks your 50 MB rule.

Removing the file in a new commit would not help, because it would stay in history. The fix is to amend `7c1d9e0` to drop the file and then run `git push --force-with-lease origin release/2.3`. I haven't done this, because it rewrites a shared branch. Two teammates fetched `7c1d9e0` this morning. After the rewrite they would need to run `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/release/2.3`, and any work they've based on that commit would need rebasing.

Two things to settle:
1. Do you approve the amend and force-push? I'd use a lease pinned to `7c1d9e0`, so it aborts if anyone has pushed since.
2. Should I warn the two teammates, or will you? The old blob may also remain on the server until it is garbage-collected, and in any PR or other ref that points at `7c1d9e0`. If the 50 MB rule covers the server's object store, someone with server access would need to clear it.

I've kept a local backup branch, `backup/task4-7c1d9e0`, which I won't push. Once you approve, I'll amend, verify no blob over 50 MB remains in the range, re-run the Task 4 test, push, and move on to the whole-plan review.
